The mixture X consists of two unsaturated cyclic hydrocarbons that decolorize bromine water and have no conjugated double bonds. Upon treatment with platinum and heat, they undergo disproportionation to form an equimolar mixture Y of two compounds that do not decolorize bromine water. Hydrogenation of both X and Y yields only cyclohexane (Z), which has a hydrogen mass fraction of 14.28% and is a common solvent. The only plausible pair for X is 1,4-cyclohexadiene (C₆H₈) and cyclohexene (C₆H₁₀), as they are non-conjugated, decolorize bromine, and upon disproportionation give benzene and cyclohexane (Y). Hydrogenation of X gives cyclohexane, and hydrogenation of Y (benzene + cyclohexane) also gives cyclohexane. The total number of hydrogen atoms in one molecule of each liquid in X is 8 + 10 = 18.

Answer: B
